# au-tax-legislation-corpus
> Two halves in one repository: `fadden`, a builder that retrieves in-force Commonwealth tax legislation from the Federal Register and turns it into retrieval material, and `tax-radar-au`, a Rust binary running a synthetic provenance-first review queue that consumes a reviewed observation contract.

## Package overview
- **Repository**: https://github.com/ryanduguid/au-tax-legislation-corpus
- **Version**: 0.3.0, released as the tag `v0.3.0`. Releases carry deterministic source archives built from Git with an SPDX 2.3 SBOM, `SHA256SUMS` and provenance attestations. They never carry a corpus or a builder wheel.
- **Licence**: release 0.3.0 is Apache-2.0 for the code. `main` and later releases are FSL-1.1-ALv2 for the code (`LICENSE`, `NOTICE`); each FSL version also becomes available under Apache-2.0 two years after it is made available. Generated corpus output is derived from the Federal Register's CC BY 4.0 material and carries its own source and licence records. The EPUBs embed the Commonwealth Coat of Arms, which the CC BY grant excludes, so the `dist` stage of the Rust `fadden` binary separates what may be redistributed from what may not.
- **Packaging**: the review queue is the standalone Rust binary `tax-radar-au` (crate `tax-radar-au` 1.0.0, built with `cargo build --locked --release`); its Python import package `tax_radar_au` was removed. The Python distribution keeps the name `tax-radar-au` and carries the builder, which is not published to PyPI and has no console script; it runs as `python -m fadden <stage>`.
- **Python**: the development checkout requires 3.14 or later. Tests run on Python 3.14 and 3.15 on Ubuntu, plus Windows 3.14 coverage for the supported live-evidence export boundary. The radar's Rust tests, Clippy and formatting run on Ubuntu and Windows.

## Corpus builder (`fadden`)
- **Stages**: `discover`, `versions`, `download`, `probe13`, `retry13`, `extract`, `pii_scan`, `pii_scan2`, `finalize`, `rates`, `check_current`, `dist`, `dist_verify`, `export_monitor_contract`, `export_publication_bundles`, `capture_register`, `export_live_evidence_bundles`, plus the separate `rulings`, `as_at`, `compare_builds` and `search` stages. `BUILD.md` documents the order and the operating boundaries.
- **Deterministic output root**: no environment variable selects it. In a source checkout the generated files live under `./corpus/`; a deployed build uses the parent of the `build/` directory holding the stage modules.
- **Privacy gates**: `pii_scan` and `pii_scan2` run before `finalize`, which refuses to run without `pii_flagged.json`. Twelve titles are disciplinary registers naming private individuals.
- **ATO rulings (`rulings`)**: fetches up to 100 named ATO-authored Legal Database documents (rulings, determinations, practical compliance guidelines, decision impact statements and edited private advice) into paragraph JSONL with the ATO reuse notice. It never touches `./corpus/` and excludes any document that matches a personal-data pattern.
- **As-at check (`as_at`)**: classifies each captured compilation against a date. `captured` is not a finding that the text was the law on that date.
- **Build comparison (`compare_builds`)**: lists the sections added, removed and changed between two local builds, matched on container and section label. It compares the derived reading view, not the authorised text, and says nothing about an amendment's legal effect.
- **Local search (`search`)**: indexes a finished corpus into one SQLite file (standard-library FTS5) after checking every row's provenance against `sources.json`, then answers full-text queries, defined-term lookups from definitions rows and section, Division and Subdivision cross-references. Every hit carries its `row_id`, compilation and Register page; none of it is authorised text.
- **Evidence contracts**: live Register capture, synthetic observations and publication candidates are distinct. A successful capture or export authorises nothing for publication.

## Review queue (`tax-radar-au`)
- **Domain**: a synthetic, provenance-first review-queue demonstration over supplied Commonwealth tax-source metadata. It does not read or store source text.
- **Supplied metadata comparison**: compares a fabricated source index, a fabricated Register-observation contract and an exact source-to-workflow map. The queue itself makes no network request and never scrapes the Register.
- **Review evidence binding**: SHA-256 source digests, run identifiers and a complete queue digest bind a human decision to the exact queue reviewed.
- **Human in the loop**: it generates deterministic change candidates. It establishes no current law, legal effect, workflow update or client action.

## What talks to the network, and when
Seven builder stages reach the Federal Register and `rulings` reaches the ATO Legal Database. Everything else, including the whole review queue, is local.
- `discover` and `versions` call the Register API about 1,100 times at 1.5 to 3 second intervals, roughly 40 minutes combined.
- `download` fetches one EPUB per title through `curl`, sleeping 10 seconds between titles to honour the Register's `robots.txt` Crawl-delay. All 946 titles take about 2 hours 40 minutes, and titles already downloaded at the same version are skipped.
- `probe13` reads version history for the titles `download` recorded as `no_epub`, and `retry13` downloads the latest published compilation for those it can recover.
- `check_current` is a read-only staleness check: 946 API calls at 1.5 seconds, about half an hour.
- `capture_register` observes every title in a manifest against the Register and retains the exact bounded HTTP 200 response bytes behind each decision. The 946-title manifest needs at least 946 requests, an enforced 1.5-second gap makes a no-retry run about 24 minutes, redirects are refused, the socket timeout is 90 seconds and each title gets at most 3 attempts. No API key is required.
- `rulings` fetches only the named targets, one request a second, HTML only, at most 8 MiB a page, from `https://www.ato.gov.au`. There is no discovery crawl.
- `as_at`, `compare_builds`, `search`, `extract`, `pii_scan`, `pii_scan2`, `finalize`, `rates`, `dist`, `dist_verify`, `export_monitor_contract`, `export_publication_bundles` and `export_live_evidence_bundles` make no request at all. The monitor and publication exporters project facts a caller has already collected.
